items.evidence: Paragraph 32 presents the applicant's contested-fraud and no-practical-effect explanation in the argument sequence.
items.scope_review: It does not establish a court rule that fraud always requires an actual appointment effect; the next standard-of-review heading is excluded.

items.evidence: Paragraph 183 says the Court decided, in the interests of justice, not to provide a final ruling on jurisdiction or reasonableness; paragraph 184 confirms no declaration would issue.
items.scope_review: Qualification: this is a reservation/non-decision holding for this dispute. Strong doubts are not a lack-of-jurisdiction holding, and the passage creates no universal bar on deciding those issues.

items.evidence: Paragraph 50 quotes Rousseau's philosophical distinctions among forms of lying.
items.scope_review: The rhetoric is neither the PSEA definition nor an adopted court elements test for fraud.

items.evidence: Paragraph 11 recounts DNR non-participation, PWGSC participation and employer submissions/support.
items.scope_review: The history creates no universal employer participation right or entitlement to receive reports.

items.evidence: Paragraph 1 states that PSEA-governed internal and external federal-public-service appointments rest on merit and non-partisanship.
items.scope_review: Qualification: the AU correctly stops before the separate private/public-sector honesty expectation. It is a PSEA staffing-values proposition, not a generalized fraud test or automatic finding.

items.evidence: Paragraph 14 describes the written reference's quality, true authorship and corroborating e-mails.
items.scope_review: These evidentiary facts are not a current-court guilt holding or reusable fraud test.

items.evidence: Paragraph 168 expressly reports what the respondent emphasized in its memorandum about two comment opportunities.
items.scope_review: The court does not adopt those opportunities as satisfying fairness; paragraph 169 immediately identifies the omitted final-analysis opportunity.

items.evidence: Paragraph 163 says the conduct can create a double-standard impression and that one may wonder about reasonable apprehension of bias; paragraph 186 later refers to apprehensions one may have as a remedy factor.
items.scope_review: Qualification: the language is deliberately tentative and provides no complete bias threshold or settled bias finding. Unresolved is preferable to forcing either a holding or fact-only hard negative.

items.evidence: Paragraph 175 narrates the corrective-action phase and anticipated agency inflexibility after its own fraud finding.
items.scope_review: It neither confirms guilt judicially nor creates a universal rule that later submissions can never cure a defect; paragraph 176 owns the case-specific cure assessment.

items.evidence: Paragraph 81 allocates PSDPA disclosure/reprisal matters to the Public Sector Integrity Commissioner and protected-disclosure reprisal complaints to the Tribunal.
items.scope_review: Qualification: this describes the PSDPA framework only. It cannot be transferred to the PSEA Commission or treated as establishing a remedy available to this applicant.

boundaries.note: Only frozen eleventh10 decisions are accepted; mutable overall progress is outside scope.
